newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran cleric denounces U.S. for backing Israel.
newsitem.headline: Iran cleric denounces U.S. for backing Israel.

text.p: A senior Iranian cleric on Friday denounced the United States for supporting Israel in what he said was a doomed Middle East Peace process.

Ayatollah Mohammad Emami Kashani, speaker the powerful Guardian Council, told a crowd of worshippers at the weekly Friday prayer meeting at Tehran University that Israel now dominated White House policy in the Middle East.
"The peace talks have come to a dead end. America is disappointed with its mediating role and now only supports Israel," the bearded Emami Kashani told the crowd who sat on prayer mats.
"The Zionist regime (Israel) has not only occupied Palestine but also occupied the White House," he said.
Emami Kashani spoke from a platform decorated with a banner of revolutionary slogans and portraits of ''martyrs'' killed during the first years after the 1979 Islamic Revolution.
The crowd, gathered on a scorching Tehran summer afternoon, chanted "Death to America" and "Death to Israel".
Approach roads to the university campus were cordoned off by police while women were separated from men by screens and by separate entrances to the university.
The Guardian Council is a body of senior clerics and Islamic lawyers with responsibility to ensure that laws passed by parliament strictly comply with the religious tenets of the Islamic republic.

The body also screened candidates who wanted to run in presidential elections in May. The elections were won by moderate Shi'ite Moslem cleric Mohammad Khatami who was sworn in as president on August 4.
Another speaker also ridiculed the U.S. for wanting to set conditions before opening talks with Iran.

"America wants to set conditions before talking to us...Mr. America, this is a dream. We will never negotiate with you," the official in charge of religious affairs at the university told the crowd before Emami Kashani's sermon.

U.S. officials have said Washington was willing to talk to Tehran's government if there was evidence that Iran would drop its opposition to the Middle East peace process and stop what they said was its support of ''international terrorism''.
Tehran has denied the ''terrorism'' charges and said U.S. authorities must unfreeze Iranian assets held by Washington since 1979 to show goodwill before any talks could begin.

Iran says Israel has no right to exist. Tehran has said the Middle East peace process is bound to fail because of the Jewish state's failure to respect the rights of Arabs and solve the Palestinian refugee problem.
